claims.statement: Delivery cleanliness is five machine counts — dirty, unpushed, stash, conflict debris and fmt — and a receipt quoting only the words `working tree clean` is not evidence; the `ok=` line must be pasted.

The cleanliness check is advisory rather than a gate: it writes no KV and blocks no other requirement, and `unpushed.count=-1` is a deliberate sentinel distinguishing an unpushed branch from a verified-equal one.

Dispatch parameters live in a git-ignored `.env.local`; the main session must source it in the same shell and map the model and thinking variables into the spawn call, never printing their values into a brief, artifact or commit.

Each subagent task runs in the background and the main session does not wait on it; a synchronous wait is allowed only when the next action strictly depends on the result and nothing else can be advanced.
